Agents in a supermarket gridworld must collect their required items and leave through the exit. Every action costs the same, so demonstrators prefer short trajectories -- unless an unknown social norm makes them behave otherwise. Your task is to propose candidate norms (obligations or prohibitions) that could explain the demonstrated behaviour.
Each demonstration is listed step by step as  `k: {atoms true in the state} action`.

Available atoms:
- at(x,y) -- the agent is at cell (x,y); x = column (0 = left), y = row (0 = top); N decreases y, S increases y, E increases x, W decreases x
- actions N, S, E, W, MOVE (any of the four moves), INTERACT (any interaction with an object: the different kinds of interaction are NOT distinguished), EXIT (leave the store; always the last action)

Output format: return ONLY a JSON list (no prose, no code fences). Each element:
{"id": short_name, "text": one-sentence natural-language statement of the norm,
 "abstraction": {"state_properties": {name: FORMULA, ...},
                 "events": {name: {"pre": FORMULA, "post": FORMULA or null}, ...}},
 "norm": {"type": "prohibition", "condition": FORMULA}
       | {"type": "obligation", "trigger": FORMULA or "START", "discharge": FORMULA}}
FORMULA := atom | name of a property/event defined in this hypothesis | {"not": F} | {"and": [F, ...]}
         | {"or": [F, ...]} | {"le"|"lt"|"ge"|"gt"|"eq": [numeric_feature, integer]}
Semantics.  A trajectory is a sequence of steps (state s_k, action a_k).  A step's label contains the atoms true in
s_k and the action a_k.  A state property is a formula over state atoms (no actions).  An event
{"pre": P, "post": Q} occurs at step k when P holds for the label of step k and Q holds in the next state s_{k+1}
(post may be null).  A prohibition counts one violation for every step whose label (including events occurring at
that step) satisfies the condition.  An obligation becomes pending at any step satisfying the trigger ("START" =
pending from the beginning) and is fulfilled by a later (or the same) step satisfying the discharge; it can be
triggered again; it is violated if it is still pending when the trajectory ends.

                 "events": {name: {"pre": FORMULA, "post": FORMULA or null}, ...}},
 "norm": {"type": "prohibition", "condition": FORMULA}
       | {"type": "obligation", "trigger": FORMULA or "START", "discharge": FORMULA}}
FORMULA := atom | name of a property/event defined in this hypothesis | {"not": F} | {"and": [F, ...]}
         | {"or": [F, ...]} | {"le"|"lt"|"ge"|"gt"|"eq": [numeric_feature, integer]}
Semantics.  A trajectory is a sequence of steps (state s_k, action a_k).  A step's label contains the atoms true in
s_k and the action a_k.  A state property is a formula over state atoms (no actions).  An event
{"pre": P, "post": Q} occurs at step k when P holds for the label of step k and Q holds in the next state s_{k+1}
(post may be null).  A prohibition counts one violation for every step whose label (including events occurring at
that step) satisfies the condition.  An obligation becomes pending at any step satisfying the trigger ("START" =
pending from the beginning) and is fulfilled by a later (or the same) step satisfying the discharge; it can be
triggered again; it is violated if it is still pending when the trajectory ends.

parsed.text: Customers are obliged to pick up the available cart at the cart depot before doing their shopping.
A customer must not walk east past the cart depot while the depot cart is still there and they do not have it.
Items should not be carried by hand inside the supermarket; they should be transported in the cart.
A customer may pick up shelf items only while in possession of the shopping cart.
After any item has been collected into the cart, the cart must eventually be returned at the counter cell before leaving.
A cart may be put down only at the designated counter location at cell (0,1).
Customers must exit on foot, without still pushing the cart or carrying items by hand.
Carts are not allowed to continue into the lower-right aisle beyond the egg shelf, so from cell (6,4) a cart must not be pushed east or south.

accepted.description: [g1_take_cart_at_depot] OBLIGED: after start, eventually pickup_cart_at_depot (before exit)  where cart_available_at_depot := cartAt(1,5); cart_depot := at(1,5); pickup_cart_at_depot := (cart_depot ∧ cart_available_at_depot ∧ PICKUP_CART) · hasCart
[g1_no_bypass_cart_depot] FORBIDDEN: (cart_depot ∧ cart_still_at_depot ∧ without_cart ∧ E)  where cart_depot := at(1,5); cart_still_at_depot := cartAt(1,5); without_cart := ¬hasCart
[g1_pickup_items_only_with_cart] FORBIDDEN: (shelf_pickup ∧ without_cart)  where without_cart := ¬hasCart; shelf_pickup := PICKUP_ITEM

[g1_return_cart_after_item] OBLIGED: after item_collected_with_cart, eventually return_cart_at_counter (before exit)  where counter_cell := at(0,1); item_collected_with_cart := (hasCart ∧ PICKUP_ITEM) · hasCart; return_cart_at_counter := (counter_cell ∧ hasCart ∧ LEAVE_CART) · cartAt(0,1)
[g1_leave_cart_only_at_counter] FORBIDDEN: (leave_cart ∧ not_counter_cell)  where counter_cell := at(0,1); not_counter_cell := ¬counter_cell; leave_cart := LEAVE_CART

[g1_no_cart_into_right_lower_aisle] FORBIDDEN: (pushing_cart ∧ ((egg_shelf_end ∧ (E ∨ S)) ∨ restricted_lower_right_cells))  where egg_shelf_end := at(6,4); pushing_cart := hasCart; restricted_lower_right_cells := (at(7,4) ∨ at(8,4))
